opening.argument: The presentation solicits paid packages ranging from $100 to €5,000 and ties earnings directly to referrals and a network bonus. It then describes commissions from purchases by people on a weaker team leg—even individuals the participant did not refer and who could be a hundred levels below—establishing a recruitment-based, tiered compensation structure. Against that backdrop, the speaker claims that a €5,030 Tycoon package can correspond to an account value of €24,000, presenting speculative appreciation as a substantial projected gain. The closing instruction is not neutral education: viewers are told to avoid missing the program and to “partner with our team today.” The paid entry, multi-level commissions, projected account value, and direct recruitment appeal together establish an active solicitation built around recruitment and tiered matrices.
